1	# The batch-06 runbook — base → research → evidence → judgment → specification
     2	
     3	Supersedes `decisions/DR-2026-08-19-research-restart-operative-instrument.md` §12.1, which
     4	`workplan/2026-09-10-road-to-batch-06.md` (B2) found stale in three ways: step 4 said "No CLI;
     5	scratch SQL" (`add-candidate` exists), step 7 ordered a hand-SQL companion UPDATE (`add-source`
     6	now takes `--url`/`--pages`/`--doi-resolution-outcome` directly — the rehearsal below applies
     7	cleanly with **zero** UPDATE statements, not one), and no step named `observe-term`, `add-term`,
     8	`add-parameter`, `adjudicate-term` or the determination engine (`scripts/assess/assess_cell.py`),
     9	none of which existed when §12.1 was written.
    10	
    11	Every command and every "expected" block below was executed for real, on a scratch copy of the
    12	canonical DB, in this same commit's rehearsal (`/tmp/rb06`), after the R10b and `next-id ref`
    13	fixes elsewhere in this commit. `sha256sum data/guidebook.db` was identical before and after.
    14	
    15	**This is a mechanics runbook, not a claim that batch 06's determination is believable.**
    16	`workplan/2026-09-10-road-to-batch-06.md`'s HEADLINE is still true after this commit:
    17	`assess_cell.gather_sources()` gathers by **slug**, not by `(ref_id, parameter_id)` — B4 is not
    18	done here. Following every step below to the letter still anchors a `stated` cell on every source
    19	linked to the slug, not on sources that actually extract the parameter under determination. Do not
    20	read a COMPLIANT gate as a sound determination; it proves the DoD's 15+ mechanical rules, which is
    21	a different claim.
    22	
    23	## Conventions
    24	
    25	- **Session id, two forms (CLAUDE.md §7).** The bare stem — `session_2026-09-10-batch-06` — is
    26	  what every `--session` flag on `db.py`/`assess_cell.py` takes and what lands in `session` /
    27	  `created_by_session` columns. The same id with `.md` appended —
    28	  `session_2026-09-10-batch-06.md` — is what `emit_data_migration.py --session`,
    29	  `citation_mining_completeness.py --session`, and the two pointer files
    30	  (`sessions/LATEST`, `sessions/LATEST-RESEARCH`) take. **Passing the wrong form does not error —
    31	  it scopes a gate to a session nothing was ever written under, and that gate passes green having
    32	  examined nothing (CLAUDE.md §5a).** Decide both forms before step 0 and never retype them.
    33	- **Scratch discipline.** `S=<scratchpad-dir>/batch06`. `cp data/guidebook.db "$S/walk.db"`; every
    34	  `db.py`/`assess_cell.py` call below is prefixed `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$S/walk.db"` **inline** — the
    35	  harness resets env between shell calls, so `export` alone does not protect a later call. Nothing
    36	  below ever opens `data/guidebook.db` for write until the final, real step 6c.
    37	- Slug used throughout: `accessible-circulation-geometry` (continuing coverage — workplan STOP
    38	  CONDITION #5 says this needs no owner decision; a *new* slug would).
    39	
    40	## Step 0 — pre-state (base)
    41	
    42	```
    43	S=<scratchpad>/batch06
    44	SESS=session_2026-09-10-batch-06
    45	mkdir -p "$S"
    46	sha256sum data/guidebook.db                                  # record; must equal step 6c's PRE value
    47	cp data/guidebook.db "$S/walk.db"
    48	python3 scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py --selftest        # SELFTEST: PASS, 19/19 (18 + R10b, this commit)
    49	GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$S/walk.db" python3 scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py --session "$SESS"
    50	```
    51	**Expected:** `--selftest` prints `SELFTEST: PASS — gate rejected the corpus AND all 19 seeded
    52	rules fired`. The empty-session probe exits 1 with **three** failures — `R1`, `R9a`, `R9b`, both
    53	of the latter reading `NOTHING IN SCOPE` — not the single `R1` DR-2026-08-19 §12.1 claimed; R9a/R9b
    54	did not exist when that line was written. Any *other* rule firing on an empty session means the
    55	session id is contaminated (reused from a prior run) — stop and pick a new one.
    56	
    57	## Step 1 — base: mint the parameter (THE SUBJECT, owner 2026-08-26)
    58	
    59	A parameter is minted from a phrase a source already uses — `observe-term` requires an **admitted**
    60	source, so step 1 borrows one already in the corpus (here `REF-00784`) purely to name the concept;
    61	this source is not thereby claimed as evidence for the cell (that comes from step 2's own
    62	admission and step 3's harvest on it).
    63	
    64	```
    65	GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$S/walk.db" python3 scripts/db.py observe-term \
    66	  --ref-id REF-00784 --surface-form "corridor clear width" --language EN \
    67	  --locator "p.4" --context-quote "minimum clear width of the corridor measured between handrails" \
    68	  --session "$SESS"
    69	```
    70	**Expected:** `{"observation_id": <N>, "created": true}`. Read `OBS` back:
    71	`select observation_id from observed_terms where surface_form='corridor clear width'`.
    72	
    73	```
    74	GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$S/walk.db" python3 scripts/db.py add-term \
    75	  --from-observation "$OBS" --canonical-en "corridor clear width" \
    76	  --rationale "names a design parameter not yet in terms" --session "$SESS"
    77	```
    78	**Expected:** `{"term_id": "TERM-0NN", "canonical_en": "corridor clear width",
    79	"adjudication_id": 1, "from_surface_form": "corridor clear width", "from_ref_id": "REF-00784",
    80	"dry_run": false}`. `add-term` itself performs the NAMES-NEW adjudication — a second, separate
    81	`adjudicate-term` call for this observation is refused (already adjudicated).
    82	
    83	```
    84	GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$S/walk.db" python3 scripts/db.py add-parameter \
    85	  --term-id "$TERM" --session "$SESS"
    86	```
    87	**Expected:** `{"parameter_id": 1, "term_id": "TERM-0NN", "canonical_en": "corridor clear width",
    88	"status": "active", "provenance": "adjudicated", "adjudicated_by": 1, "outcome": "NAMES-NEW",
    89	"dry_run": false}`. Record `parameter_id` — every later step keys on the integer, not the term id.
    90	
    91	## Step 2 — research + evidence: search, admit, stage
    92	
    93	```
    94	GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$S/walk.db" python3 scripts/db.py log-search \
    95	  --slug accessible-circulation-geometry --language EN \
    96	  --query-text "corridor clear width wheelchair" --engine pubmed --depth-method scoping \
    97	  --session "$SESS" --target-tier 1 --target-evidence-type clinical --target-scope high_control \
    98	  --prior-expectation "expect a handful of anthropometric studies" \
    99	  --results-found 3 --results-screened 3 --results-admitted 0 --mining-direction none
   100	```
   101	**Expected:** `{"exec_id": <E>, "slug": "accessible-circulation-geometry", "admitted": 0,
   102	"dry_run": false}`.
   103	
   104	**Mint the ref_id — never by hand (CLAUDE.md §4).**
   105	```
   106	REF=$(GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$S/walk.db" python3 scripts/db.py next-id ref | python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['next_id'])")
   107	```
   108	**Expected:** `REF-NNNNN`, one past the live high-water mark. This is the fix landing in this same
   109	commit (item 3) — before it, `next-id` offered only `{connections,gaps,terms,conflicts}` and
   110	`add-source` refused any hand-picked id by *naming* `dbcore.next_ref_id(conn)` rather than a
   111	command to run.
   112	
   113	```
   114	GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$S/walk.db" python3 scripts/db.py add-source \
   115	  --ref-id "$REF" --author "Smith|Jane" --year 2020 --title "..." --tier 1 \
   116	  --doi 10.9999/... --evidence-type clinical --scope high_control \
   117	  --metadata-quality COMPLETE --verification-status VERIFIED --verification-method tool \
   118	  --verified-by-tool crossref --doi-resolution-outcome RESOLVED \
   119	  --slug accessible-circulation-geometry --local-ref-id 1 --session "$SESS"
   120	```
   121	**Expected:** `{"ref_id": "REF-NNNNN", "linked_slug": "accessible-circulation-geometry",
   122	"dry_run": false}`. **`--verification-status` is a CLI choice of `{VERIFIED,UNVERIFIED}` but the
   123	column itself accepts NULL if the flag is omitted — always pass it.** Since this commit, omitting
   124	it (or admitting a URL-bearing source with it left NULL) fails the gate's new `R10b`, which exists
   125	because that exact condition is what wakes the scheduled `verify-urls` cron and pushes a DB blob to
   126	`main` (workplan B3). No companion hand-SQL UPDATE is needed: `--url`, `--pages`, and
   127	`--doi-resolution-outcome` are all real flags today.
   128	
   129	```
   130	GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$S/walk.db" python3 scripts/db.py add-candidate \
   131	  --exec-id "$E" --found-under-slug accessible-circulation-geometry \
   132	  --disposition PENDING-VERIFICATION --title "..." --session "$SESS"
   133	```
   134	**Expected:** `{"candidate_id": "<N>", "dry_run": false}`. `--disposition` is live vocabulary off
   135	the column's own CHECK — `ADMITTED|MISCELLANEOUS|OUT-OF-SCOPE|PENDING-VERIFICATION|REHOME`; a
   136	value outside that set is refused with the CHECK spelled out, nothing written.
   137	
   138	## Step 3 — evidence: harvest the concept AS THE SOURCE WRITES IT (D-0173)
   139	
   140	```
   141	GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$S/walk.db" python3 scripts/db.py observe-term \
   142	  --ref-id "$REF" --surface-form "clear passage width" --language EN \
   143	  --locator "Table 2" --context-quote "clear passage width for a manual wheelchair user" \
   144	  --session "$SESS"
   145	```
   146	**Expected:** `{"observation_id": <N2>, "created": true}`. Verbatim, unjudged — R11's "harvest at
   147	evidence" half. `research_batch_dod.py`'s `R11-harvest` fails any admitted source with zero
   148	`observed_terms` rows, so this step is not optional on a real batch.
   149	
   150	## Step 4 — judgment: adjudicate the harvested phrase (D-0173)
   151	
   152	```
   153	GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$S/walk.db" python3 scripts/db.py adjudicate-term \
   154	  --observation-id "$N2" --outcome NAMES-EXISTING --term-id "$TERM" \
   155	  --rationale "same concept as corridor clear width" --session "$SESS"
   156	```
   157	**Expected:** `{"adjudication_id": <N>, "outcome": "NAMES-EXISTING", "contested": false}`.
   158	`--outcome` is live vocabulary from the column's own CHECK (`NAMES-NEW|NAMES-EXISTING|NOT-OURS|...`);
   159	`NAMES-EXISTING`/`NAMES-NEW` require `--term-id`, refused otherwise. This is the crossing step
   160	owner ruling 2026-08-27 assigns to judgment, not evidence — the phrase was only *recorded* at step
   161	3; here it is decided.
   162	
   163	**Also judgment: grade population-of-study vs population-served (R13).**
   164	```
   165	GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$S/walk.db" python3 scripts/db.py add-population-match \
   166	  --ref-id "$REF" --target-population MOB --study-population "manual wheelchair users n=30" \
   167	  --match-grade EXACT --session "$SESS"
   168	```
   169	**Expected:** `{"match_id": "<session>-<ref>-<pop>", "dry_run": false}`.
   170	`--target-population` is a `populations.population_code` (the identity lens; codes AND names, per
   171	CLAUDE.md §6 — never bare axis codes). `db.py add-population-match` does **not** enforce
   172	uniqueness on `(ref_id, population)` — that refusal is deliberately absent (CLAUDE.md §4); a
   173	second, dissenting grade lands as a second row on purpose.
   174	
   175	**Also research: the citation-mining pass R2 requires (a deferred one still counts).**
   176	```
   177	GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$S/walk.db" python3 scripts/db.py log-mining \
   178	  --slug accessible-circulation-geometry --ref "$REF" --direction backward \
   179	  --deferred-reason "mining deferred to next pass" --session "$SESS"
   180	```
   181	**Expected:** `{"logged": true, "connections": 0, "dry_run": false}`.
   182	
   183	**Also research: R1's Co-1 pass (a genuine, well-formed zero-yield satisfies it).**
   184	```
   185	GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$S/walk.db" python3 scripts/db.py log-search \
   186	  --slug accessible-circulation-geometry --language EN \
   187	  --query-text "wheelchair corridor width DPO lived experience" --engine web \
   188	  --depth-method scoping --session "$SESS" --target-tier 1 --target-evidence-type co1 \
   189	  --prior-expectation "expect little" --results-found 0 --results-screened 0 \
   190	  --results-admitted 0 --mining-direction none \
   191	  --findings-note "genuine absence in index searched"
   192	```
   193	**Expected:** `{"exec_id": <E2>, "slug": "accessible-circulation-geometry", "admitted": 0,
   194	"dry_run": false}`. A zero-yield row with **no** `findings_note` fails R14 — the note is what
   195	distinguishes "well-formed, nothing there" from "the query itself was broken."
   196	
   197	## Step 5 — specification: the engine determines ONE cell
   198	
   199	```
   200	GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$S/walk.db" python3 scripts/assess/assess_cell.py \
   201	  --db "$S/walk.db" --emit-sql "$S/cell.sql" --parameter-id "$PID" \
   202	  --slug accessible-circulation-geometry --identity MOB \
   203	  --session "$SESS" --stamp "2026-09-10 00:00:00" --report-json "$S/cell.json"
   204	```
   205	**Expected (stdout):**
   206	```
   207	param 1×MOB      stated       basis=T1+CO1+T2   scale=population refs=6 rso=0 cfo=0 sha=<12 hex>
   208	
   209	1 cell(s) determined; SQL artifact: <S>/cell.sql
   210	REPLAY through emit_data_migration.py -> migrate_db.py, never by hand.
   211	```
   212	`--stamp` is an INPUT, never `now()` — the engine run twice on the same inputs must be byte-
   213	identical (verified separately; not part of this walk). `cell.sql` holds 8 `INSERT`s: 1
   214	`convergence_assessment` (synthesis), 1 `specifications` (specification), 6
   215	`specification_source_links` (the junction — H01/H02 need both the JSON and the junction row per
   216	entry, not just `governing_refs`).
   217	
   218	**⚠ HAZARD — do not apply `cell.sql`.** `assess_cell.py` wrote those 8 rows straight into
   219	`$S/walk.db` (the scratch DB it ran against). Step 6a's `emit_batch_sql` diffs that *same* scratch
   220	DB against canonical, so `batch.sql` **already contains** every row `cell.sql` contains, alongside
   221	everything steps 1-4 wrote. Feeding `cell.sql` into `emit_data_migration`/`migrate_db` as well is
   222	a double-insert: reproduced in this commit's rehearsal, it fails
   223	`UNIQUE constraint failed: convergence_assessment.convergence_id` on replay. `cell.sql` is a
   224	by-product for eyeballing the engine's own SQL; discard it once `--report-json` and the printed
   225	line have been read.
   226	
   227	**⚠ HAZARD — no re-determination path.** `idx_spec_row_identity` is a UNIQUE index on
   228	`specifications(parameter_id, COALESCE(identity_code,''), COALESCE(icf_code,''),
   229	COALESCE(needs_code,''), COALESCE(medical_code,''))`. Running `assess_cell.py` a second time for
   230	the *same* parameter × lens combination is refused at apply time, not at engine time — the engine
   231	happily re-emits, and the refusal surfaces only when `migrate_db.py` tries to INSERT. Batch 06 is
   232	the first determination of this cell; a batch 07 that revisits it needs a supersede design (an
   233	owner decision this runbook does not make — workplan DELIBERATELY WAITING).
   234	
   235	## Step 6 — apply: capture, migrate, gate, regenerate — in that order
   236	
   237	**6a — capture the delta out of the scratch DB (not the engine's own file, per the hazard above).**
   238	```
   239	python3 scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py \
   240	  --scratch "$S/walk.db" --canonical data/guidebook.db --out "$S/batch.sql"
   241	```
   242	**Expected:** `Wrote <S>/batch.sql — 23 insert(s), 0 update(s)` (counts will differ with different
   243	inputs; what matters is that the per-table breakdown printed includes exactly one
   244	`specifications` insert and one `convergence_assessment` insert — the step-5 rows, captured here
   245	and nowhere else).
   246	
   247	**6b — name the migration file. `--session` takes the `.md` form.**
   248	```
   249	python3 scripts/emit_data_migration.py \
   250	  --session "$SESS.md" --summary "batch 06: accessible-circulation-geometry parameter x MOB" \
   251	  --input "$S/batch.sql" --output-dir scripts/migrations
   252	```
   253	**Expected:** prints the new path, `scripts/migrations/data_<timestamp>_2026-09-10-batch-06.sql`.
   254	Rehearse this against a throwaway `--output-dir` first if unsure; only point it at
   255	`scripts/migrations` once ready to apply for real.
   256	
   257	**6c — apply. This is the ONLY canonical write of the session (CLAUDE.md §3).**
   258	```
   259	python3 scripts/migrate_db.py --session "$SESS.md"
   260	```
   261	**No `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH` override — this is the one call in the whole walk that is meant to touch
   262	`data/guidebook.db`.** Rehearse it first against a scratch copy of canonical
   263	(`cp data/guidebook.db "$S/replay.db"; GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$S/replay.db" python3
   264	scripts/migrate_db.py --session "$SESS.md"`) and confirm `pragma foreign_key_check` is empty and
   265	`sha256sum data/guidebook.db` is unchanged before running it for real.
   266	**Expected:** `Done. Schema at version <N>; 1 data migration(s) applied.`
   267	
   268	**⚠ HAZARD — regenerate BEFORE the gate, not after.**

   271	```
   272	Run this immediately after 6c and before step 7. `pipeline_completeness_fresh` and
   273	`evidentiary_audit_fresh` are both **blocking** `--check` gates against the tools' own output
   274	files; skipping this step or running it after the gate leaves those files stale against the DB
   275	migrate_db.py just changed, and both go red on the very next check run.
   276	
   277	## Step 7 — gate
   278	
   279	```
   280	python3 scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py --session "$SESS"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# regenerate_derived.sh — regenerate every DB-derived output the CORRECT way, then verify.
#
# Lesson (2026-07-24): a dashboard was regenerated with `python3 tool.py > out.html`, which
# captured the tool's stdout STATUS LINE instead of its HTML — the tools write their own
# output path (DEFAULT_OUT). The `> redirect` is always wrong here; call the writer, no redirect.
# This script is the single sanctioned regeneration entry point after ANY data/guidebook.db change.
#
# Each generator writes its own file(s); we then run the tools' own `--check` gates (what CI runs)
# to prove the committed tree now matches a fresh regeneration. Exit non-zero if anything is stale.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

python3 tools/pipeline_completeness.py
python3 tools/evidentiary_audit.py

echo "== Verifying --check gates (mirror CI regenerate-*.yml) =="
python3 tools/pipeline_completeness.py --check
python3 tools/evidentiary_audit.py --check

echo "All DB-derived outputs regenerated and --check-clean. Review 'git status' and commit."

All work done on scratch copies. **`git status --porcelain data/guidebook.db` is empty and `sha256 = dfda5f3b…5e5bf` is unchanged** (verified at start and end). The only dirty files are the harness's own `transcripts/` and `scratchpad/…/commands.jsonl`, which the harness writes. I used `grep -r`/`git grep` via Bash for anything that could live under `.ignore`d paths (`sessions/`, `versions/`, `_archived/`, `transcripts/`).

---

## A. The R4 replacement text

**Executed:** parsed both `.claude/settings.json` blobs and diffed the `printf` argument lists token-by-token.

Survives, on its own terms:
- Only R4's lines changed. 62 → 63 args, one `replace` opcode; `hooks.SessionStart` = 1 entry with 2 hooks before and after; `hooks[1:]` byte-identical; all non-`hooks` settings identical. **No other rule's hook text moved.**
- Cost: 3544 → 3676 chars, **+132** (~33 tokens/session). Not a real cost.
- D-0170's four lenses and the `NOT (item x population)` warning are both still there, verbatim.
- The new sentence is *accurate* against `scripts/migrations/071_parameter_at_base.sql:96-137`: `specifications.parameter_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES base_parameters`, four lens columns, `CHECK (COALESCE(identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, medical_code) IS NOT NULL)`, `idx_spec_row_identity` UNIQUE on exactly those five. And against the rulings themselves, read directly: `references/project-standards.md:1311-1322` (2026-08-26, subject) and `:2484-2546` (2026-08-28 + the D-0182 "at least one" supersession).
- `grep -r "open owner decision"` across the whole tree including `.ignore`d dirs: the only live-surface hits left are unrelated ("owner decision #10" in `.github/CODEOWNERS`) and one historical narration at `references/project-standards.md:2571`. The sweep is genuinely clean.

**But the enforcer was not swept, and it is in the file this commit edited.**

```
scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py:45   R4  COMBINATORIAL dimension.  Cells are (item x population); …
scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py:373  f"(evidence_population_match). Cells are (item x population): a search that "
```

Line 373 is a **runtime FAIL message printed to the session**. So the SessionStart hook now tells every session `NOT (item x population)… THE KEY IS RULED`, and the gate that enforces R4 tells them, on failure, `Cells are (item x population)`. That file's own docstring (`:26-28`) says: *"If it and `governance/research-contract.yaml` ever disagree, the contract governs and this table is the thing to correct."* The commit added 43 lines to that file, nine of them into that very docstring table (the R10b block at `:75-82`, immediately below R4's entry), and left R4's entry stating the retired key. `research_contract_sync --check` cannot see it — it compares rule *ids* and the generated hook string, never the enforcer's prose (`scripts/generate/research_contract_hook.py:136`).

Two further live surfaces still teach it: `governance/evidence-architecture.md:114`, `governance/pipeline-operations.md:28`. The workplan's B6 lists the two *skills* as owed but never lists the DoD's own R4 text — so this one is not tracked anywhere.

Caveat worth stating: the hook now asserts the key is ruled, while `scripts/assess/assess_cell.py` still takes `--slug` as a **required** argument and gathers by it. The runbook discloses this at lines 15-21; the hook — which is what every session actually reads — does not.

## B. R10b, adversarially

**Executed:** six scratch copies of canonical, one row inserted into `evidence_sources` in each, `research_batch_dod.py --session ADV` run against each.

| case | fires? | correct? |
|---|---|---|
| url + `verification_status='UNVERIFIED'` | **no** | ✓ UNVERIFIED is a real value |
| url NULL + status NULL | **no** | ✓ |
| url `''` + status NULL | **no** | ✓ `COALESCE(url,'') <> ''` |
| url set + status NULL | **YES**, exit 1 | ✓ |
| url `'   '` + status NULL | YES | ✓ matches `verify_urls.py:417` `url != ''`, same pool |
| url + status NULL, **different session** | no under `--session`; **YES** under `--all` | see below |

The predicate is right, and "admitted" matches the rest of the gate: R10b uses `scope.replace('session','created_by_session')` on unaliased `evidence_sources`, exactly as R10 (`:545,549`) and R11 (`:590,592`) do; R9a/R9b use the aliased `e.created_by_session` equivalent (`:484`). Same definition.

The B3 mechanism reproduces: `verify_urls.py:417/438` pool on `url != '' AND verification_status IS NULL`; `EXEMPT_TABLES = ("evidence_source_authors", "pipeline_runs")` (`scripts/audit/migration_reproducibility.py:72`) does not contain `url_verification_runs`; `.github/workflows/verify-urls.yml:19` is `cron: "0 06 1,15 * *"`.

**Live corpus: 9 sources, all `VERIFIED`, all with URLs. R10b hits = 0. It passes today.**

Two defects:

1. **R10b passes vacuously.** `ok("R10b", "no admitted source carries a URL with verification_status left NULL")` — no subject count. Run against a session that admitted nothing, it prints a bare PASS. I ran it: `--session NO_SUCH_SESSION` printed `R10b: PASS` on the same run where `R9a`/`R9b` printed `NOTHING IN SCOPE` and `R11`/`R11-harvest` printed `EXAMINED: 0`. This is CLAUDE.md §5(a), and it is the *first* item in that file's own DESIGN RULES block, and it was written six lines below the two rules hardened against exactly it (`:487-491`, "SUBJECT COUNT FIRST. Adversarial pass 2026-08-23 found R9a/R9b printing a bare PASS for a session that admitted nothing").

2. **R10b is enforced but not in the contract.** `governance/research-contract.yaml` has no R10b, so the SessionStart hook does not warn any session about it — a session learns of it by being failed. The comparator that is supposed to catch precisely this (`research_contract_hook.py:136`, `re.findall(r"\bR(?:1[0-5]|[1-9])\b")`) cannot match `R10b`: `\b` does not fire between `0` and `b`. `--check` prints `PASS: contract and enforcer agree on 15 rule ids` — it never saw the new rule. (Pre-existing shape: R9a/R9b are invisible too.)

3. Minor: the R10b comment cites `verify_urls.py:447-470` for the pool. 447-470 is the empty-candidate guard; the pool is `:415-445` and the `INSERT INTO url_verification_runs` is `:471`.

## C. `next_ref()`

Clean. `scripts/db.py:101-108` → `connect(readonly=True)` = `dbcore.connect` (`db.py:78`), which opens `mode=ro` + `PRAGMA query_only` at `db_path()`, i.e. **honours `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH`** (`dbcore.py:83-96`). It calls `dbcore.next_ref_id(conn)` and returns it — zero duplicated logic. Verified equal on the scratch: CLI `{"next_id": "REF-00979"}` vs direct `dbcore.next_ref_id(conn)` = `REF-00979`. Single connection to a single file, so there is no table `next_ref_id` unions that this connection cannot see — `ref_id_homes` (`dbcore.py:220-229`) reads `sqlite_master` on that same handle.

**But the defect the commit names as the reason is still there.** Commit message: *"add-source's own refusal message sent an operator to `dbcore.next_ref_id(conn)` instead of a command."* That message is unchanged:

```
scripts/db.py:2377-2378   "Get the next one from `dbcore.next_ref_id(conn)`, which computes …"
scripts/db.py:3633        "Mint with dbcore.next_ref_id()."
scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py:528   "mint above dbcore.next_ref_id(conn), …"   ← in a file this commit edited
skills/citation-miner_SKILL.md:191,222 ; skills/research-log-manager_SKILL.md:135
```

The command now exists and nothing points at it. The subcommand is added; the stated motivation is unresolved.

## D. The runbook — followed literally, end to end

Fresh scratch (`cp data/guidebook.db $S/walk.db`), `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH` inline on every call, using **only** what the runbook says.

**Reproduces exactly:** step 0 (`SELFTEST: PASS … all 19 seeded rules fired`; empty-session probe = exactly three failures, `R1`/`R9a`/`R9b`, the latter two `NOTHING IN SCOPE`); step 1 (`observation_id 34`, `TERM-089`, `parameter_id 1`); step 2 (`exec_id 44`, `REF-00979`, `candidate_id 76`); steps 3-4; **step 5 verbatim** — `param 1×MOB stated basis=T1+CO1+T2 scale=population refs=6 rso=0 cfo=0 sha=23d3a3467ed1`, and `cell.sql` holds exactly 8 INSERTs, 1 `convergence_assessment` + 1 `specifications` + 6 `specification_source_links`.

**Hazard 2 reproduces, exactly as stated.** Feeding `cell.sql` through `emit_data_migration` → `migrate_db` alongside `batch.sql`:
```
sqlite3.IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed: convergence_assessment.convergence_id
```
**Step 7 reaches COMPLIANT**, 19 rules PASS, real exit 0 (run against the post-migration replay copy, which is byte-equivalent to what canonical would be after 6c).

**Hazard 3 reproduces.** I could not run `regenerate_derived.sh` (it writes `tools/`, `audits/`) so I ran the two blocking gates it verifies, read-only, against the post-migration DB:
```
canonical (pre-migration):  pipeline_completeness --check exit 0 ; evidentiary_audit --check exit 0
replay.db (post-migration): pipeline_completeness --check exit 1 "STALE" ; evidentiary_audit --check exit 1
```
Both are `level: blocking` in `governance/check-registry.yaml`. The ordering claim holds. (Pedantic: they are irrelevant to step 7's `research_batch_dod`; the gate that goes red is `run_checks.py`.)

### Defects found by following it

1. **`workplan/2026-09-10-batch-06-runbook.md:242` — the stated expected output is wrong for its own inputs.** Runbook: `Wrote <S>/batch.sql — 23 insert(s), 0 update(s)`. Actual, from the runbook's literal command sequence: **22 insert(s), 0 update(s)**. The hedge at `:242` ("counts will differ with different inputs") does not apply — the inputs were the runbook's own. I cross-checked that nothing was silently dropped: per-table row deltas between `walk.db` and canonical sum to **22**, and `batch.sql` captures **22**, with zero tables where delta ≠ captured. So there is no 23rd row and no reader can reconstruct where the number came from.

2. **`:243-244` — "the per-table breakdown **printed**" does not exist.** `emit_batch_sql.py:173` prints one line only. The per-table breakdown is written as `-- <table>: N insert(s)` **comment lines inside the output file** (`:139`). A session told to check the printed breakdown has nothing to check.

3. **`:227-233` — HAZARD 4's mechanism is false.** It states: *"refused at apply time, not at engine time — the engine happily re-emits, and the refusal surfaces only when `migrate_db.py` tries to INSERT."* Executed, twice:
   - re-run on the same scratch: `sqlite3.IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed: index 'idx_spec_row_identity'` at `assess_cell.py:721`, uncaught traceback, exit 1.
   - the actual batch-07 shape — fresh copy of the *post-migration* canonical, new session, new stamp: **same crash**, exit 1, and `--emit-sql` is never written (`cell3.sql` does not exist).
   
   The engine does not "happily re-emit". The refusal is at **engine time**, at step 5, as a raw traceback, on a scratch DB the engine has already partially written. A batch-07 session planning around this hazard as written will plan for the wrong failure at the wrong step.

4. **`:262-265` — the 6c safety rehearsal cannot be performed as written.** The runbook says rehearse with `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$S/replay.db" python3 scripts/migrate_db.py`. But `migrate_db.py:42` reads `MIGRATIONS_DIR` from `GUIDEBOOK_MIGRATIONS_DIR`, which the runbook never names — so the rehearsal only finds the migration if 6b already wrote it into the repo's `scripts/migrations/`, which contradicts 6b's own "rehearse against a throwaway `--output-dir` first". To stay read-only I had to find `GUIDEBOOK_MIGRATIONS_DIR` myself, outside the runbook. That is a gap in the one step the runbook flags as the only canonical write.

5. **Unbound shell variables.** `$S` is `<scratchpad>/batch06` (placeholder); `$SESS` is set at step 0; `$REF` is the only other one given an assignment recipe (`:106`). `$OBS` (`:75`), `$TERM` (`:85`), `$E` (`:131`), `$N2` (`:154`), `$PID` (`:201`) are used and never assigned. I had to read each back out of the previous JSON.

6. **`:70-71` gives raw SQL with no runner.** *"Read `OBS` back: `select observation_id from observed_terms where surface_form='corridor clear width'`"* — CLAUDE.md §4 says **there is no `sqlite3` CLI**. No Python snippet is offered, and the value was already in `observe-term`'s own JSON output two lines above.

7. **`:114-127` — the worked `add-source` example is a template for CLAUDE.md §5(c).** It admits `--doi 10.9999/... --verification-status VERIFIED --verification-method tool --verified-by-tool crossref --doi-resolution-outcome RESOLVED` for a fabricated DOI, and the gate passes it (R9a/R9b/R10 all PASS). The runbook mentions `retrieval_log.py`, `--verify-authors`, `scratchpad/CURRENT` and `preserve_transcripts.py` **zero times** (`grep -c` = 0). CLAUDE.md §5(c) says *"Verification must leave an artefact: `scripts/research/retrieval_log.py` persists every payload"* — the runbook's evidence-admission step has no such step, and its caveat at `:15-21` is about `gather_sources`, not about manufactured verification standing. Also: its `add-source` example passes no `--url`, so the runbook's own walk never exercises the R10b this same commit added.

8. **`:286` is a paraphrase presented as reproduced output.** `R1..R15, R9a, R9b, R10b: PASS (19 of 19)` — the tool prints 19 separate detailed lines and never emits the string `19 of 19`.

9. **`:169` — `{"match_id": "<session>-<ref>-<pop>"}` is not the shape.** Actual: `session_2026-09-10-batch-REF-00979-MOB`. `db.py:3435` uses `session[:24]`, so the session is truncated. (Harmless — `db.py:3437-3441` suffixes on collision — but the documented template hides it, and two sessions sharing a 24-char prefix would look identical.)

## E. The attestation

`attestations/decisions_DR-2026-08-19-research-restart-operative-instrument.json` **validates** against `schemas/attestation.schema.json` (I ran `jsonschema.validate`), and `adherence_log_audit.py --check presence|schema|evidence --base c7d24bf^ --head c7d24bf` is green on all three, `EXAMINED: 1`. The free text **does** describe what was done, in specifics, not a restatement of the rule — it names B2's three staleness findings and the replacement. That part is good. Two problems:

CLAUDE.md rule 2 notes **no gate reads the free text for meaning** — so this sentence is load-bearing precisely because only a human will ever check it, and it does not hold.

The runbook's own step 8 (`:311-314`) tells the next session the rule: *"one attestation file per artifact path, **updated via its `reattestation` log**, never duplicated."* The commit did not follow the advice it wrote. (Its "same convention as the existing 2026-08-25 entry" claim is literally true — that entry is the same shape — but the precedent predates nothing that makes it right.)

Not owed: a new `attestations/<slug>.json`. The artifact path is unchanged, so a second file would be the duplication step 8 forbids. A `reattestation` entry plus a moved `doctrine_sha` was the shape.
